system:
You filter search results. For each candidate, decide whether it actually addresses the subject of the clinician's question.

A candidate that merely shares wording with the question, or that belongs to an unrelated part of hospital operations, does not address it. A candidate that addresses the subject in different words does.

Keep a candidate when genuinely unsure: wrongly discarding relevant knowledge is worse than showing one extra item.
prompt:
QUESTION: How do we prevent central line infections?

CANDIDATES:
[C1] Antibiotic Stewardship Program §1 Program Leadership and Accountability
Program Leadership and Accountability The ASP must have a physician leader (infectious disease physician preferred) and a pharmacist leader with stewardship training. Leadership must have the support and accountability of hospital administration. The program must report to the infection control committee and QAPI.

[C2] Infection Control and Prevention §4 Surveillance & Reporting
Surveillance & Reporting Ongoing surveillance of HAIs must be conducted. Reportable conditions must be submitted to appropriate public health authorities within required timeframes.

[C3] Infection Control and Prevention §5 Isolation Procedures
Isolation Procedures Contact, droplet, and airborne precautions must be implemented appropriately. Signage, dedicated equipment, and private rooms (when available) must be utilized.

[C4] Infection Control and Prevention §3 Sterilization & Disinfection
Sterilization & Disinfection All reusable medical equipment must be properly decontaminated, cleaned, and sterilized or high-level disinfected according to manufacturer instructions and facility protocols before use on another patient.

[C5] Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §10 Skin Antisepsis with Chlorhexidine Gluconate (CHG)
Skin Antisepsis with Chlorhexidine Gluconate (CHG) Open the CHG 2% applicator (ChloraPrep). Apply to insertion site and surrounding skin using a back-and-forth scrubbing motion for a minimum of 30 seconds. Apply to an area of at least 3–4 cm radius around the insertion site. Allow to air dry completely — MINIMUM 30 seconds for CHG; do NOT fan, blow, or blot dry. CHG MUST be completely dry before a

[C6] Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §5 Open Sterile Supplies Using Aseptic Technique
Open Sterile Supplies Using Aseptic Technique Open the dressing change kit and all supplies onto a clean, dry surface using aseptic non-touch technique. Do NOT contaminate the inner sterile field. Open CHG applicator, Biopatch, and TSM dressing packaging and place on the sterile field without touching sterile surfaces with ungloved hands.

[C7] Central Line Dressing Change DETAILED §1 Verify Order and Assess Need
Verify Order and Assess Need Confirm a physician order for central line dressing change (or that the change is per standing protocol). Assess dressing: is it due by schedule, or is it soiled, loose, lifting, bloody, or non-occlusive? Any of these conditions require immediate dressing change regardless of schedule.

[C8] Hand Hygiene DETAILED §2 BEFORE a clean or aseptic procedure
BEFORE a clean or aseptic procedure Before any invasive procedure, sterile technique, or contact with a non-intact skin site. Examples: inserting IV/urinary catheter, wound care, oral care, medication preparation at bedside, handling sterile equipment. Perform hand hygiene immediately before donning sterile gloves.

The infection prevention and control program reflects the scope and complexity of the hospital services provided by addressing all locations, patient populations, and staff. **Attributes:** ESP-1 **Crosswalk:** §482.42(a)(4), §482.42(a)(4), §482.42, §482.42

The hospital’s governing body ensures that the problems identified by the infection prevention and control program are addressed in collaboration with hospital quality assessment and performance improvement leaders and other leaders (for example, the medical director, nurse executive, and administrative leaders).
